notes: Rock armour (riprap) around the whole island edge, built by tools/lib/shoreline-generation.mjs into the chunk records and generated/world/shoreline.json. Always-on scenery, not a switchable street-detail layer.

Every value here is an estimate for game art (production inference), read from the dated photos (Sep 2025 Street View, Commons Aug 2021 and May 2025, the reference notes named per segment), the 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial (Esri World Imagery levels 12-19, 0.34 m; the 0.15 m level-20 exports a06/a07 show the 2025-08-29 capture) and the USGS 3DEP 2023 DEM; none is survey data.

Segments and closures cover the island outline w26767313 end to end, by distance s_m along it (start > end runs across the outline's start, s = 0). A segment takes the OSM breakwater polygon (man_made=breakwater, material=rock) of its source_key. Its part inside the outline, from the crest to the outline, is draped on the land as a terrain overlay with no collision, overlay_bias_m above the land: the verge at the top of the riprap (the 'verge' ground cover: dry grass and dirt), with a few low cobbles set in it at the outline. land_ground stays the only support there, so route QA, the regional anchors and boundary recovery are unchanged. Two segments that meet join into one pile and one slope; a segment that meets a closure ends in a rock face.

Outside the outline a flat shoulder shoulder_m wide continues the verge's ground cover in its shading (the dirt and small stones in front of the rocks in the photos), its inner edge at the height of what is drawn inside (the riprap overlay, or the land where no breakwater lies). Behind it the underlay rises into the crest's core (slope.berm): over inner_m to below_crest_m under the segment's lowest crest rise, flat for width_m (varying along the shore over wavelength_m) and falling drop_per_m, so the crest stones bedded on it stand as high above the verge as the photos show and the gaps between them show core, not water; then it runs down past the water plane (y -0.12) to toe_y_m. Two segments' crests blend over joint_blend_m either side of their joint; at a capped end (a pier, ramp or the causeway beside it) the core sinks to the land over cap_taper_m. The DEM's gradient between dem_fit_m along each cross-section, clamped to gradient_m_per_m (the photographed 1.5:1 to 2.5:1) and smoothed over gradient_smoothing_m, with the land's height sets a waterline for a core of waterline.core_m; that waterline, its plan points smoothed over waterline.smoothing_m either way so the band's edge has no jogs and no corners from the outline's own, then sets each cross-section's fall (within waterline.gradient_m_per_m); relief_m of boulder-scale bumps fades in over top_blend_m behind the shoulder. Where a cross-section meets the outline again within its toe plus clamp_reach_m (the 0-9 m slit the OSM outline cuts into the north-west shore), its profile is squeezed into the inlet and falls to the land on the far side. A segment with crest_rows false (that slit's seaward edge) is only the lower slope of a crest another segment builds: no shoulder, no core, no crest rows, and its own cobble rule. The underlay shows between the stones, dark in the gaps near by, and stands in for them at the heap's apparent tone as they thin out with distance.

Stones are one shared set of fractured quarry blocks (prototypes, cycling through block, slab, long, wedge and chunky shapes): convex polyhedra with flat broken faces, sharp corners and edges, shallow creases across the big faces and chipped corners (12-20 faces; the clean block is the coarse LOD); stones under pebbles.below_m use pebbles, clean blocks without the creases and chips, and stones of big.above_m or more only the irregular big.families (a big clean block or slab reads as a box), each instance scaled uniformly by its size (its longest side) and dumped: resting on a broad face (posture) against the underlay's own surface there (flat on the shoulder and the core's top, tilted on the fall), turned any way and tilted up to tilt_deg, then lowered where its underside would hang over the underlay. A top row just outside the outline (inner faces at least setback_m beyond it, about the player's radius), a back row piled within depth_m behind it and crest_fill stones between them make the crest one continuous low heap, as high and as dense as each segment's photos show (its crest_rise_m above the land edge for the back row, the top row at most 5 cm more, the crest fill in proportion; crest_fill_scale times the rows' fill); small chink stones packed between the crest's blocks over the core (chink: lying flat, tops rise_m above the core, tucked under their neighbours by overlap); a few small shoulder stones in the shoulder; small blocks tumbled along a ramp's foot over the cut's face (ramp_foot); a heap packed over the slope to toe_extra_m past the toe, largest size class first, its small class only within small_reach_m of the outline (the upper slope the player sees close; lower down the voids stay dark); from just above the waterline out only stones that stand at least 0.3 m clear of the water and show no more than past_water_m beyond it are kept, so the band's edge stays where it is when the stones thin out; and a few low cobbles (small stones mostly buried in the dirt) inside the band within reach_m of the outline, rising at most top_m above the land, so the player walks over them. No stone reaches more than a quarter of its size past a capped segment end, and none overhangs a ramp's cut. A segment may set its own cobble fill, reach_m and size_m (west_wedge: the sliver beyond the north-west slit, densely set with flat-topped stones so it reads as the stone it is in the aerial). Weathered driftwood logs lie sunk into the stone tops on the face below the crest (from_waterline_m up from the waterline), with stone under most of their length, and washed-up planks at the waterline. Everything is visual only; structures (piers keep the slope under them, slipways cut it) clear the stones by clearance_m, except stones that top out under_drop_m below the land edge under a pier, paths clear the cobbles, and the street-detail hard shapes (spawn, ferry path, QA route, stairs, doors, approaches) clear everything. Stones are batched per section_m of shore, band and shape. The shader thins them out one by one with distance (thinning: a stone drops out at its own share, start to 1, of its reach, size times reach_per_m within [min_m, max_m]); each batch is culled only beyond the farthest reach of its stones from the batch's centre, so no batch edge ever shows, and the underlay's stand-in follows the share of the heap still drawn (fitted to the stones as the document's lod.underlay_fade_m). The logs keep a fixed range, wood_m [end, margin].

Closures: kind wall is a concrete face under the land edge (coping_m above it) down to wall_bottom_y_m, for pier and platform edges the photos show as vertical; kind ramp is a boat ramp, a slab running out from the land edge at ramp_grade to ramp_bottom_y_m between side walls ramp_wall_m high; kind none builds nothing (the causeway's Yerba Buena context terrain, or the inlet the next segment's clamped slope fills).

Mounds: a rubble mound standing out in the water where a segment's breakwater runs out as a jetty (the north tip's w26767328): a flat-topped ridge along centerline_xz, its crest crest_y_m high with a slight crown, its sides falling at gradient to toe_y_m; each side's waterline lies at the breakwater polygon's edge (bounded by half_width_m), which sets the crest's width (at least crest_min_m); over taper_m at its far end the crest sinks under the water. Big blocks lie flat on the crest and the heap's size classes on the sides; a ramp cuts it as it cuts the shore. Its records and batches belong to the segment, numbered from section 100.

Tones: each segment's stones and underlay take a palette from tones.palettes, [brightness, warm share, dark share, pale share] of the shader's stone families (charcoal, brown-grey, olive-grey a tenth, pale weathered, the rest plain grey), sampled from the dated photos: charcoal along the north-west and west (refs/sv 02, 04, 05, ph01; dark grey to black), grey-tan in the east and south (16, 18, 20, 13, 11; lighter grey with tan faces), brown-grey at the Sailing Center and the north tip (31, 25, 21). At each end a segment's tone blends over blend_m (at most the segment's length) half way into its neighbour's, across a closure too, so the two meet at the joint without a switch. The underlay stands in for the stones in the same tone, so a segment keeps its tone into the far band.

Rock grounds: land that is stone in the aerial (the sliver beyond the north-west slit: all the land within the outline from s_m[0] to s_m[1], closed by the chord back). The flat breakwater overlay lies over the verge there, drawn as the riprap's bare rock, at the heap's tone. Bare parts of the underlay (the fill of a clamped inlet, a capped end's face, the cut beside a ramp, the edge of a segment without crest rows) are shoreline-face records in the same rock, not the dark gaps of a heap.

rock_grounds.reason: The sliver of land the OSM outline splits off the north-west shore. It stands where the riprap's seaward slope stands in the aerial (the DEM falls across it from about 2.7 m to 1 m), and the player can walk it, so it stays land drawn as stone: the slope of the one crest beside the slit, not a verge between two walls.
rock_grounds.reference: 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial (Esri level 19) tile t0250 and plot a05-west-hairpin: one band of stone from the path to the water, the outline's three lines inside it; Street View contributor May 2024 (refs/sv 04, s150/s450): one crest of dark angular stone seen from the path

segments.reason: The north-west shore below the Gateview and Bayside housing, from the small concrete structure at the north-west corner past the island's westernmost point to the tip of the sliver the OSM outline splits off the shore; runs across the outline's start (s = 0).
segments.reference: Street View contributor panoramas, May 2024 (John Ewing, from the shore path; refs/sv 01 s4800, 02 s5100, 03 s0, 04 s150, 05 s700, 26 s4708): a continuous crest of dumped angular grey and grey-tan stone 0.4-1.2 m, 0.3-0.8 m above a dry-grass or gravel verge, barely above the grass at s0; the 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial tiles t4750, t5000, t0000 and t0250 show the band with surf at its foot

segments.reason: The seaward edge of the sliver the OSM outline splits off the north-west shore (its slit, s 308-450, runs back up inside it): in the aerial the whole band from the shore path to the water is one riprap slope, so the crest runs along the slit (segment west fills it) and this edge is only the slope's foot: no crest rows, the heap down from the sliver's edge to the water; the sliver itself is a rock ground, set with low flat-topped stones.
segments.reference: 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial (Esri level 19) tile t0250 and plot a05-west-hairpin: one band of stone from the path to the water, the outline's three lines inside it; Street View contributor May 2024 (refs/sv 04, s150/s450): one crest of dark angular stone 0.5-0.8 m above the grass

segments.reason: The west shore from the head of the OSM slit (its clamped slope fills the slit) past Cityside Park and the ferry plaza to the causeway, the first shore a ferry arrival sees; contains the step 1b pilot (s 1380-1740).
segments.reference: Cityside: Street View official Jan 2023 (refs/sv 06, before the park: a low crest of mixed brown and grey stone 0.5-1 m above a bare strip, water right behind) and a contributor place photo of Sep 2025 (Cityside refs ph01: a planted crest running up to dark angular riprap); ferry plaza: ferry-shelter refs, Sep 2025 Street View 12-sv-road-sw-zoom (83 Treasure Island Rd), Sep 2026 29-sv-water-ne from the float, Commons c01 and c08 (Aug 2021) and c10 (May 2025); 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial tiles t0250-t1750; USGS 3DEP 2023 profiles: crest 3.2-3.9 m NAVD88, 2:1 to 3:1 to the water

segments.reason: The causeway's east flank and the south shore along the Treasure Island Yacht Harbor in Clipper Cove, to the small concrete pier w1222505174.

mounds.reference: Street View contributor May 2024 (John Ewing; refs/sv 22 and 23): a long, low, flat-topped mound of grey angular stone, its crest about 1-2 m above the water, curving out from beside the boat ramp, waves breaking on its outer face; 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial (Esri level 19) plot a04-north-tip: the mound about 10-12 m wide over about 115 m. Its dark marker post near the end is not built (known gap).
